reconstructed_theorem_text: Let E and V be arbitrary real normed vector spaces, let s be any subset of E, let f and g be functions from E to V, let c be a function from the real numbers to E, let t₀ be a real number, and let v belong to E. Suppose that f and g are each Fréchet differentiable at c(t₀), that c is differentiable at t₀ with derivative v, that c(t) belongs to s for every t in some neighborhood of t₀, and that there is a neighborhood U of c(t₀) such that f(x) = g(x) for every x in U ∩ s. Then the Fréchet derivatives of f and g at c(t₀), applied to v, are equal: Df(c(t₀))[v] = Dg(c(t₀))[v].
